title: Pilot study on the acquisition of suspicious skin lesions with thermography and photography in patients at the Dermatology Clinic of the University Medical Center in Göttingen
summary: When examining the skin for suspicious changes as part of skin cancer screening, the result is heavily dependent on the experience and training of the examiner. This procedure is also time-consuming and expensive. This pilot study uses thermal cameras and digital cameras to examine the differences between moles suspected of being cancerous and healthy skin. The aim is to determine the differences in temperature between malignant moles and healthy skin. Adult patients who present with suspicious moles or already have confirmed skin cancer will be included. For this purpose, the suspicious areas are photographed with thermal and digital cameras and background information is collected. If an altered mole or confirmed skin cancer has to be surgically removed, cell samples of the tissue will be made available for further examination in the cell laboratory.

interventions.name: Patients with suspicious lesions or already diagnosed skin cancer who present to the outpatient clinic of the Dermatology Clinic undergo standardized thermographic and digital photographic imaging of lesion sites and, possibly contralateral, unaffected areas of skin. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Dermatology patients attending the clinic for clarification of skin lesions suspected of being malignant, or patients who have already been diagnosed with skin cancer before starting treatment
Exclusion criteria:
Patients who are unable to give consent due to a relevant pre-existing condition (e.g. dementia) or those who do not understand the content of the patient information and consent.
